items.description: The shared agent identity line: the agent's initials (or its picture) on the agent's palette colour, the name, and — when the host reports one — the activity state as an icon, a WORD and a tone. Every agent visualization (lanes, graph, fan-out, handoff, presence roster) renders this component, so an agent looks the same wherever it appears and its state is never colour-only information (WCAG 1.4.1). The colour comes from AgentRef.ColorIndex, which is normalised into the eight-slot palette --tm-agent-color-0 … --tm-agent-color-7; the ink painted on it is --tm-agent-color-ink, whose AA (4.5:1) contrast against every slot is measured in both themes by AgentColorTokenTests. The picture is host data: AgentRef.AvatarUrl is loaded only when it is an absolute http(s) source (the package's image allowlist, the same rule the markdown pipeline applies to images) and a refused target falls back to the initials instead of becoming a live source or a broken image. The badge is NOT a live region, carries no aria-live and never moves (no transition, no animation): the surface that owns the run has exactly one announcement channel, and a pulsing badge would become a second one while re-introducing motion that prefers-reduced-motion would have to cover. Naming: with the name visible the badge has no aria-label at all — the visible text IS the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3); with ShowName=false the composed avatar becomes one role="img" graphic named by the agent and, when one is rendered, its state, because an aria-label on a role-less span is ignored by assistive technology. An unknown state value renders no chip, so a stale contract can never paint a wrong verdict, and a whitespace name renders the localized "Unnamed agent" fallback instead of an empty gap.

parameters.name: Agent
parameters.description: The agent to show. Null renders nothing at all — a surface that has not loaded its snapshot yet must not paint an anonymous avatar. The record is a VALUE: a host recomposes it with `agent with { … }`.

parameters.name: Status

items.notes: The badge is deliberately not interactive: it renders no button, no tab stop and no drag surface, so WCAG 2.5.7's non-drag alternative and the 44 px coarse-pointer target do not apply to it — a host that makes a whole row clickable keeps that obligation on its own row. Its CSS declares no transition or animation, which keeps the package's reduced-motion enumeration unchanged; a future animated subject has to add its own prefers-reduced-motion block. Under Windows high contrast the avatar opts out of the system palette (forced-color-adjust: none) so the eight agent fills stay distinguishable and keeps a CanvasText border for the circle's edge.

items.description: Agents, the tools they call, the resources they read and the human in the loop as ONE drawn network: a box per node in the column its kind belongs to, a curve per connection whose thickness is how often it was called, and a short pulse on the curve every time a new call arrives. The surface renders the SNAPSHOT it is given plus the incremental calls the host streams in, and never polls, fetches or mutates anything: the host owns the transport and the component owns its view. The injected TimeProvider drives both the pulse window and the paint throttle, so a test with a fake clock controls the whole surface. The layout is pure C# (AgentGraphLayout): columns follow the node kind (human, agent, resource, tool) and are then tightened so every edge points forward, a cycle is broken deterministically and its closing edge is routed BELOW the boxes, rows inside a column are ordered by a barycenter heuristic so the curves stop crossing, members of a group stay in one contiguous run, and the stroke width is a LOG scale over the call count so a quiet connection stays visible beside a busy one. A host may pin a node exactly (NodePositions) and the canvas grows to contain it. The drawing is never the only way to read the graph: the scrollport (a div, the ONE role=group, named by the localized "Agent graph" and described by its instructions) wraps a plain unlabelled SVG whose nodes are native BUTTONS (one roving tab stop, ARROW keys walking the real connections, Home/End on the edges, Enter/Space activating natively), and the View switcher renders the SAME data as two plain tables. Exactly ONE polite live region announces a selection, a zoom change, a lost selection and a stream hole; the only animated subject is the call pulse and its prefers-reduced-motion block keeps a still highlight instead of the movement.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture the "last call" time formats in. Null uses CultureInfo.CurrentCulture. It never changes the values, only their shape.

parameters.name: DetailTemplate
parameters.description: The host's detail surface for the selected node — the full label, the call numbers, links, actions. Rendered in a role=region named by the localized "Node detail". Null renders no detail at all.

parameters.name: Events
parameters.description: The incremental calls applied ON TOP of Snapshot, in any order. The shared AgentEventStream sorts them, drops what was already applied and rejects a batch with a hole (raising OnGapDetected), so a host may pass the same batch twice, or a cumulative list, without de-duplicating itself. Null means the snapshot is all there is.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2-6. Default 3.

parameters.name: MaxPulses
parameters.description: How many edges may pulse at once. Default 6. A burst of calls from a fan-out agent must not light up the whole picture, so only the NEWEST pulses survive: an older one is retired as soon as the cap is exceeded.

parameters.name: MaxZoom
parameters.description: The largest allowed scale. Default 2.5 (250 %).

parameters.name: MinZoom
parameters.description: The smallest allowed scale. Default 0.5 (50 %).

parameters.name: NodePositions
parameters.description: The nodes the HOST pinned, by node id (a hand-placed sketch, a restored layout). A pinned node keeps its exact coordinate and the canvas grows to contain it; everything else is still laid out around it. Null pins nothing.

parameters.name: OnGapDetected
parameters.description: Raised once per batch that contains a HOLE — with the first sequence the stream does not have. The documented repair is the host's own: load a new snapshot and pass it (with its sequence) as Snapshot.

parameters.name: PulseDuration
parameters.description: How long one pulse stays on its edge. Default 600 ms. The highlight is removed by a timer on the injected TimeProvider, so a fake clock closes it without sleeping; under prefers-reduced-motion the same window keeps a STILL highlight instead of the animation. The value is also written onto the root as --tm-agent-graph-pulse-duration, so the CSS animation and the timer share ONE length and a host that changes this parameter never has to restyle the knob.

parameters.name: RenderThrottle
parameters.description: The paint-gate window for event-driven updates. Null uses the shared AgentRenderThrottle.DefaultInterval (100 ms); TimeSpan.Zero paints every batch. The STATE is never throttled, only the paint.

parameters.name: SelectedNodeId
parameters.description: The selected node's id, two-way bound with SelectedNodeIdChanged (@bind-SelectedNodeId). The matching node carries aria-pressed="true" and its neighbours are highlighted; with DetailTemplate set the node's detail renders in a named region below the surface.

parameters.name: SelectedNodeIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new selected node id when the reader selects a node (a null value clears it).

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowZoom
parameters.description: Whether the zoom controls are rendered. Default true. They are the WCAG 2.5.7 alternative to the pinch gesture, so a host is expected to keep them unless its own chrome zooms.

parameters.name: Snapshot
parameters.description: The COMPLETE state of the graph at one moment: the nodes, the connections between them and the calls each connection carried, plus the sequence the snapshot includes. The component never mutates it. Null renders the localized empty state (the surface is usable before the host's first load lands).

parameters.name: TimeProvider
parameters.description: The clock the pulse window and the paint throttle measure on. Null uses the container's TimeProvider and falls back to TimeProvider.System — the host's clock always wins over the machine's.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Agent graph"); the heading also names the drawing, so the name a reader hears is the one they see.

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: Which presentation is shown, two-way bound with ViewModeChanged. Default Graph; Table is the text alternative with exactly the same data.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new presentation when the reader uses the View switcher.

parameters.name: Zoom
parameters.description: The scale of the drawing, two-way bound with ZoomChanged. Default 1 (100 %), clamped into MinZoom-MaxZoom. A host that pins it keeps control: the reader's zoom reports the change and the next render from the host decides.

parameters.name: ZoomChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new scale when the reader zooms (a button, "fit", or a pinch/ctrl+wheel gesture).

parameters.description: Additional HTML attributes applied to the root element.

items.notes: Keyboard: the node is a NATIVE <button> inside a <foreignObject>, so Enter and Space activate it exactly once with no emulation, and the roving tabindex keeps the whole graph ONE tab stop while the scrollport stays tabindex=-1 (programmatically focusable, never a second stop in front of the nodes). ARROW keys move along the actual EDGES (the neighbour furthest in that direction wins, then the cross-axis distance, then the painting order) and never along the declaration order; Home/End jump to the first and the last node. The page scroll an ARROW may produce is accepted rather than suppressed — a render-time @onkeydown:preventDefault cannot be per-key and would swallow Tab and the button's own native activation (the same decision TmTabs and TmTopBar document). Focus: a selected node the host removes clears the selection and hands the focus back to the viewport instead of dropping the reader onto the body. Pointer: panning is NATIVE scrolling of the viewport (a mouse, a wheel, a scrollbar and the keyboard all work), and the package's tm-agent-graph.js only imports the CORE pointer-gesture.js helper for pinch/ctrl+wheel zoom plus the two-finger pan delta — there is no second drag implementation and no <script> tag. Pulses: a call lights its edge up for PulseDuration on the injected TimeProvider (the same value is written onto the root as --tm-agent-graph-pulse-duration, so the CSS animation and the timer share one length), at most MaxPulses at a time (the newest win), and the ONE animated subject has a prefers-reduced-motion block that removes the movement while keeping a dashed, Highlight-toned highlight. Fit-to-view measures the scrollport (the same module) and keeps the current zoom when nothing can be measured (prerender, no JavaScript), so it never jumps to a guess. High contrast: forced-colors hands the curves, the group boxes and the arrow heads (an SVG fill the system palette does not remap) to CanvasText, selection and approval to a Highlight BORDER and focus to its own thicker OUTLINE, so a focused node is never mistaken for a selected one (WCAG 2.4.7), and every dim is dropped (opacity 1) instead of lowering system-colour contrast. A dimmed node is a TOKEN change rather than an opacity, because it is still an active button whose label has to keep its contrast. Every user-facing string (including the accessible names of the nodes, the table headings and the zoom read-out) comes from ITmLocalizer.

items.description: A run handed from agent to agent as ONE chain: a labelled step per handoff — who handed what to whom, when, how the receiving agent answered — with the things that travelled and the things that were lost (and why) behind a Details button on every step, plus a chain-wide loss summary that names what the run actually dropped. The surface renders the steps it is given and never polls or mutates anything: the host owns the handoff data and the transport, the component owns its view. The step ordering is the host's own chain order — the component never reorders, filters or invents a step. Accessibility: the chain is an ordered list of labelled steps, every status and every item kind is an ICON plus a localized WORD plus a tone (colour is never the only carrier, WCAG 1.4.1), and the passed/lost lists live in a region a native <button> opens and closes with aria-expanded and aria-controls — no key emulation anywhere (docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md). The table view carries exactly the same facts without the geometry, so a screen-reader, keyboard-only or phone reader loses nothing. ONE polite live region speaks only when a step the reader was on disappears from the host's data and the focus has to move.

A host that pins the list keeps control: the reader's toggle reports the new set and the next render decides.

items.description: A multi-agent run as one LANE per agent on a shared time axis (default 600 px per hour — ten pixels per minute, the scale an agent run is read at): a block per piece of work, the review verdict a block carries (an icon AND a localized word), handoff arrows between the lanes and the current moment as a vertical line. The surface renders the SNAPSHOT it is given plus the incremental events the host streams in, and never polls, fetches or mutates anything: the host owns the transport and the component owns its view. The injected TimeProvider drives both the live now line and the paint throttle, so a test with a fake clock controls the whole surface. The layout is pure C# (AgentLanesLayout): the range is derived from the blocks (an open block reaches now), padded and aligned to a nice tick step from a fixed ladder, overlapping work inside one lane is stacked into sub-rows instead of covering itself, a block whose agent the snapshot does not declare still gets a lane (appended, with the localized fallback name) so a run is never silently incomplete, and an unresolvable handoff is counted instead of guessed. The timeline is never the only way to read the run: the View switcher renders the SAME layout as two plain tables, every block is a native button named by its visible activity FIRST and then by its agent, kind, time, state and marker, and the component owns exactly ONE polite live region (a selection, a zoom change and a stream hole). Events go through the shared AgentEventStream: ordered, idempotent and contiguous, so a batch with a hole is rejected whole, reported to the host (OnGapDetected) and announced instead of painting stale data. The paint gate (AgentRenderThrottle, 100 ms by default) collapses a burst of events into one trailing paint while the STATE absorbs every event. The surface declares no transition and no animation.

items.notes: Geometry: the timeline is the ONE horizontal scrollport (overflow-x auto, overflow-y hidden) and the agent column and the time axis are sticky, so a phone never scrolls the page sideways. "Very short block" + coarse pointer: the block is widened to the 44 px touch target visually, while its axis position and the table's exact timestamps stay authoritative. "Fit to width" measures the scrollport through the package's tm-agent-lanes.js module (the same module that imports the CORE pointer-gesture.js helper for pinch/ctrl+wheel) and keeps the current zoom when nothing can be measured (prerender, no JavaScript), so it never jumps to a guess. A host that pins ViewMode, SelectedBlockId or PixelsPerHour keeps control: the reader's change is reported and the next render from the host decides. The component declares no transition and no animation — a live run repaints while it streams, so a moving surface would animate for the whole run.

items.description: One agent run, live: what it is doing right now, how long it has been going, what it has cost, and the timeline of the steps that got it here. The strip answers those four questions without opening anything — the current step, a clock that ticks only while the run is running, the cost so far and the steps' timeline with a glyph and a hidden kind word per step. A host that supplies PendingApproval gets its decision surface in its own named region between the metrics and the timeline; an approval that appears is also announced in the component's polite live region. Collapsed folds the strip into one status bar that keeps the essentials and drops the timeline; a pending decision is never hidden by the fold. The run title, the current step and the step text wrap at narrow widths while only the short elapsed/cost/model values keep one line, so the strip reflows at 320 px. The monitor renders the snapshot it is given and never polls anything.

parameters.name: AllowCollapse
parameters.description: Whether the strip may be folded at all. Default true. false removes the toggle and keeps the strip expanded even when Collapsed is pinned true — a bar a host cannot reopen is not a feature.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the strip when ShowTitle is false. Defaults to the localized "Agent monitor".

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Collapsed
parameters.description: Whether the strip is folded into its status bar, two-way bound with CollapsedChanged. Default false. The bar keeps the state, the title, the current step, the clock, the cost and a pending-approval marker; the timeline and the approval slot need the room. A host that pins the parameter keeps control.

parameters.name: CollapsedChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new collapsed state when the reader presses the toggle.

parameters.name: CompletedAt
parameters.description: When the run finished. Null while it is still running; a finished run stops its clock and keeps its recorded duration.

parameters.name: CostFormatter
parameters.description: Formats the run's cost given in MICRO-UNITS. Null uses AiCostFormatter with Culture — the culture's own currency.

parameters.name: CostMicroUnits
parameters.description: What the run has cost so far, in MICRO-UNITS (1,000,000 is 1.00 of the currency). Null renders the cost metric with an em dash, so an unreported cost never reads as free.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the cost. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time. The clock-style duration is not localized on purpose.

parameters.name: EmptyContent

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: IconResolver
parameters.description: Maps a step's AgentStepKind to an icon name. Null uses the component's own mapping (thinking → a spark, a tool call → a terminal, an approval → a shield, …). The kind's WORD is always rendered for a screen reader, so an override never removes the only copy of the information.

parameters.name: PendingApproval
parameters.description: The host's decision surface for a pending approval — an approve/reject pair, a link, a short form. It renders in its own role="group" named by the localized "Waiting for your approval", between the metrics and the timeline. Null renders no approval region at all.

items.description: The agent's plan of steps: what it intends to do, reviewed and edited before the run and watched while it runs. In Review mode a step can be renamed inline (F2 or a click on its title, Enter saves, Escape cancels), added below a row or at the end, removed with an Undo strip, and reordered through the core TmSortableList. In Running mode the same rows are read-only, a running step counts its live elapsed time from the injected TimeProvider, the summary adds the plan total ("4 of 7 done · 1:24"), and a failed step shows its error and offers "Retry from this step". The component never mutates Steps: every edit raises OnPlanChanged(newSteps, edit) and the host applies it.

parameters.name: AllowEditing
parameters.description: Whether the plan may be edited at all. Default true — and only meaningful in AgentPlanMode.Review, because a running plan is read-only regardless. Set false for a review that may only be read and approved.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the plan. Null names it by the rendered heading — so the name a reader hears is the one they see — and, without a heading, by the localized "Agent plan".

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes for the root element.

parameters.name: EmptyContent
parameters.description: Rendered instead of the localized "No steps yet." when Steps is null or empty. The plan's instructions and its live region stay rendered either way.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3, so the plan can sit under any page outline; the level has no effect when ShowTitle is false.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Whether the plan is being reviewed or is running. Default AgentPlanMode.Review. A Running plan is read-only — no rename, no add, no remove, no reorder and no Approve / Run — but it keeps the live timer of a running step, the summary, a failed step's error and its Retry action.

parameters.name: OnApprove
parameters.description: Raised when the reader approves the plan. The action is rendered only when this callback is bound, so a plan without a host decision has no dead button. Review mode only.

parameters.name: OnPlanChanged
parameters.description: Raised once per edit with the WHOLE proposed step list and the AgentPlanEdit that produced it. The component does not apply the edit itself; the host stores the list and the next render shows it. Not raised for a rename that changed nothing, for a refused empty title, or for a reorder that did not move a row.

parameters.name: OnRetryFrom
parameters.description: Raised with the failed step whose Retry the reader chose: the host restarts the run FROM that step (the steps before it keep their state). Available in both modes, because a failure is reported while the run is going.

parameters.name: OnRun
parameters.description: Raised when the reader starts the run. Rendered only when this callback is bound. Review mode only — a running plan offers no second start.

parameters.name: ShowSummary
parameters.description: Whether the "4 of 7 done · 1:24" summary is rendered next to the title. Default true; the summary is the only place the plan's whole progress and total elapsed time are stated.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true; set false when the host page already provides the section heading. The plan stays named through AriaLabel either way.

parameters.name: Steps
parameters.description: The plan, in display order. The component renders exactly this list (plus the inline rename editor) and never writes back to it: every edit is reported through OnPlanChanged, so a host that ignores the callback keeps the plan it passed. Null renders the empty state.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the plan. Null renders the localized default ("Plan"). The heading is not rendered when ShowTitle is false.

examples.title: Review a plan and start the run
examples.code:
<TmAgentPlan Steps="@steps"
             OnPlanChanged="ApplyAsync"
             OnApprove="ApproveAsync"
             OnRun="RunAsync" />

@code {
    private IReadOnlyList<AgentPlanStep> steps = [
        new("Draft the outline"),
        new("Confirm the sources"),
        new("Publish the summary"),
    ];

    private Task ApplyAsync(IReadOnlyList<AgentPlanStep> next, AgentPlanEdit edit)
    {
        steps = next; // the host owns the plan; the component only proposes
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }
}

items.description: The run of an agent as a treegrid: one row per agent, sub-agent, tool call or step, with the state, the model, the elapsed time, the cost and the tokens of each — and, on a parent row, the total of everything under it (marked as a summary and named in full for a screen reader). The nodes are a FLAT list and the tree comes from AgentRunNode.ParentId: an orphan hangs under the root and is marked, a parent cycle is rejected instead of hanging the grid, and a duplicate id is read once. The component never mutates Nodes: it renders the host's snapshot and owns only the reader's view state (the filter, the collapsed rows and the selection when the host does not bind it). The surface is a role="treegrid" with one roving tab stop, APG tree keys, Enter/Space selecting, and one polite live region for its own events. A name or model cell clipped to one line inside the grid carries its whole text in a title, so a host that renders no DetailTemplate still has a full-text path.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name of the treegrid. Null names it by the rendered heading — so the name a reader hears is the one they see — and, without a heading, by the localized "Agent run tree".

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: CostFormatter
parameters.description: Formats a cost given in MICRO-UNITS (1,000,000 is 1.00 of the currency). Null uses AiCostFormatter with Culture — the culture's own currency, with micro-unit precision below one hundredth of a unit.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the costs and the token counts. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time. The durations are clock-style (m:ss) on purpose and are not localized.

parameters.name: DetailTemplate
parameters.description: The detail panel of the selected node, rendered in a named region below the grid. Null renders no detail panel — the grid alone is a complete surface.

parameters.name: EmptyContent
parameters.description: Rendered instead of the localized "No nodes yet." when Nodes is null or empty. The component's instructions and its live region stay rendered either way.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: Nodes
parameters.description: The run, as a flat list. The tree is built from AgentRunNode.ParentId; the component never mutates this list. Null or empty renders EmptyContent or the localized empty sentence instead of an empty treegrid.

parameters.name: SelectedNodeId
parameters.description: The selected node's id, two-way bound with SelectedNodeIdChanged (@bind-SelectedNodeId). The matching row carries aria-selected="true" and the detail region renders when DetailTemplate is supplied. A host may keep the component uncontrolled: the reader's selection is then internal and still renders the detail.

parameters.name: SelectedNodeIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the newly selected node id (a row click, Enter or Space).

parameters.name: ShowCost
parameters.description: Whether the cost column is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowFilter
parameters.description: Whether the "show only" control is rendered. Default true; the filter still applies when the host pins ShowOnly without the control.

parameters.name: ShowModel
parameters.description: Whether the model column is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowOnly
parameters.description: Which nodes the reader wants to see, two-way bound with ShowOnlyChanged (the built-in "show only" control raises it). The filter keeps the ancestors of every row it keeps. Default AgentRunFilter.All.

parameters.name: ShowOnlyChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the reader picks another value of the "show only" control.

parameters.name: ShowTime
parameters.description: Whether the elapsed-time column is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true; set false when the host page already provides one. The grid stays named through AriaLabel or the localized default.

parameters.name: ShowTokens
parameters.description: Whether the tokens column is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: TimeProvider
parameters.description: The clock the live timers read and schedule from. Null (the default) uses the registered TimeProvider and falls back to System — the parameter exists for a host (and a test) that wants a different clock than the app-wide one.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: An optional heading above the grid. It also becomes the grid's accessible name when AriaLabel is not set.

items.description: The prompt composer of an AI conversation: an autosizing textarea whose Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a new line (an IME composition never sends), a send slot that becomes Stop while a generation runs, attachment chips with MaxAttachments/MaxFileSize enforced against a localized message, a model selector (built-in or the host's own template), an opt-in voice input that renders only where the Web Speech API exists, and one suggestion listbox shared by the "/" slash commands and the host's "@" mention provider. The textarea is the combobox of that listbox (aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, arrow keys, Enter, Escape) and keeps the DOM focus while the list is open, the caret position comes from the package's ES module ai-composer.js (which also owns the autosize and the IME guard), and every announcement goes through the component's single polite live region. OnSubmit carries the trimmed text, the attachments, the selected model, the mentions and the slash command; the draft is cleared only after the handler completed.

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Accepted file types forwarded to the browser picker (for example "image/*,.pdf").

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: Accessible name of the prompt. Default null uses the localized "Message". Set it when the page has several composers so a screen-reader user can tell them apart.

parameters.name: Attachments
parameters.description: Attachments seeded by the host. A new list whose ids differ from the current chips replaces them; echoing the list the component raised through AttachmentsChanged is not a replacement.

parameters.name: AttachmentsChanged
parameters.description: Raised with every accepted attachment change (a pick, a removal, the post-submit clear).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Commands
parameters.description: Slash commands offered after the reader types "/". A command is filtered by its title (and its description); picking one inserts its Prompt (or "/{Title}") into the draft and the next submit carries it as AiComposerSubmit.Command.

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Disables the prompt, the picker, the voice control and the send/stop slot.

parameters.name: EnableAttachments
parameters.description: Offer the attachment picker and the chip list. Default true.

parameters.name: EnableVoiceInput
parameters.description: Offer the opt-in voice input. Default false: the control renders only when this is true AND the browser exposes the Web Speech API, so a browser without speech recognition never shows a dead button.

parameters.name: IsGenerating
parameters.description: Whether a generation is running. The send slot renders the Stop control instead of Send while it is true, and Enter cannot start a second generation.

parameters.name: MaxAttachments
parameters.description: How many files one prompt may carry. Default 5. A zero (or negative) value refuses every file with the localized "at most 0 files" message, which is how a host turns attachments off without removing the picker.

parameters.name: MaxFileSize
parameters.description: The largest file the composer accepts, in bytes. Default 10 MB. Zero (or negative) disables the size check; the browser and the host's upload path remain responsible for what they will actually read.

parameters.name: MaxRows
parameters.description: How many rows the prompt may grow to before it starts scrolling. Default 8. The module clamps the autosize to this row count, and a value of zero or less leaves the height uncapped.

parameters.name: MentionDebounce
parameters.description: Quiet period before a mention query is sent. Default 200 ms. Zero sends every keystroke, which is only reasonable for an in-memory provider.

parameters.name: MentionProvider
parameters.description: The source of the "@" mentions. The composer calls it with the typed query, debounced by MentionDebounce and cancelled as soon as the query changes or the list closes. Without a provider the "@" trigger does nothing.

parameters.name: Models
parameters.description: The models the reader may pick from. An empty (or null) list hides the built-in select unless ModelSelectorTemplate supplies a picker of its own.

parameters.name: ModelSelectorTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in model select with the host's own picker — a full model picker with descriptions, a provider switcher, … The host binds its own control to SelectedModel; the composer only carries the value into the submit.

parameters.name: OnStop
parameters.description: Raised when the reader activates the Stop control of a running generation.

parameters.name: OnSubmit
parameters.description: Raised with the submitted prompt: the trimmed text, the attachments, the selected model, the mentions the draft references and the slash command it started from. The draft, the attachments and the recorded mentions are cleared only after the handler completed — a handler that throws keeps the reader's text. Without a bound handler the send control is not offered.

parameters.name: Placeholder
parameters.description: Placeholder of the prompt. Default null uses the localized "Ask anything…".

parameters.name: SelectedModel
parameters.description: Identifier of the model the draft targets, two-way bound through SelectedModelChanged. A host echoing the value it received is not a replacement.

parameters.name: SelectedModelChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the model the reader picked in the built-in select.

parameters.name: SpeechLanguage
parameters.description: BCP-47 language of the speech recognizer. Default null uses the document's language and then en-US.

parameters.name: Sticky
parameters.description: Stick the composer to the bottom of its scroll container at every width. Default false — the narrow (mobile) layout is sticky on its own, this forces it in a wide container too.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description: The draft. Two-way bound: the component raises TextChanged on every edit and clears the draft after a successful submit. A host that reassigns the value to something the component did not type replaces the draft (the suggestion list closes and the recorded command/mentions are dropped); a host echoing the value it received is not a replacement.

parameters.name: TextChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the draft on every edit and with an empty string after a successful submit.

parameters.name: TrackVirtualKeyboard
parameters.description: Track the on-screen keyboard so a sticky composer stays above it (the iOS visualViewport pattern of TmChat.TrackVirtualKeyboard). Default false: no viewport listeners and no inline knob.

examples.title: Send a prompt and stop a running generation
examples.code:
<TmAiComposer @ref="composer"
              @bind-Text="draft"
              IsGenerating="@generating"
              OnSubmit="@SendAsync"
              OnStop="@(() => generation?.Cancel())" />

@code {
    private TmAiComposer composer = default!;
    private string draft = string.Empty;
    private bool generating;
    private CancellationTokenSource? generation;

    private async Task SendAsync(AiComposerSubmit submit)
    {
        generation = new CancellationTokenSource();
        generating = true;
        try
        {
            await client.AskAsync(submit.Text, submit.Attachments, submit.Model, generation.Token);
        }
        finally
        {
            generating = false;
        }
    }
}

              Accept="image/*,.pdf"

items.description: The transcript of an AI conversation plus the streaming machinery around it: a focusable role=log live region that renders the host's turns through TmAiMessage (or a host MessageTemplate), the empty state with the host's suggestion prompts, an optional render window for a very long history, the "Load older messages" control, the floating "New messages" and "Stop generating" pills, and the polite completion note. StreamAsync folds an IAsyncEnumerable<AiStreamDelta> into the message the host appended, throttles the renders through the injected TimeProvider (a Server circuit must not re-render per token), keeps the partial answer on Stop and marks the turn Completed, Stopped or Failed. Auto-scroll follows new content only while the reader is at the bottom — a detached reader gets the "New messages" pill instead of a moving viewport — and the scrolling surface is the package's ES module ai-conversation.js (scroll tracking plus a ResizeObserver on the content), so smooth scrolling follows prefers-reduced-motion.

parameters.name: AutoScroll
parameters.description: Follow new content and offer the "New messages" affordance. Default true. When false the component imports no browser module at all and never scrolls — the host owns the scrolling surface.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: CSS length of the transcript (for example "32rem" or "100%"). Default null uses the stylesheet's height.

parameters.name: Messages
parameters.description: The turns of the conversation, oldest first. The host owns the list: append a turn before it starts streaming and the component renders it. Reassigning the property to a NEW list instance is treated as loading another conversation (the render window snaps to the newest turns); appending to the same instance keeps the window where the reader left it.

parameters.name: MessageTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in TmAiMessage of every turn. The template receives the message, so a host can attach its own per-turn actions (regenerate, feedback, retry) without the conversation re-declaring them.

parameters.name: OnStop
parameters.description: Raised once after a running generation was stopped — by the built-in Stop control or by a host calling StopAsync(). The component cancels the token it handed to the stream itself, so this is a notification, not a request: a handler must not call StopAsync() again (it is a no-op, so it cannot loop).

parameters.name: OnSuggestion
parameters.description: Raised with the text of an activated suggestion prompt. The chips render only while the conversation has no turn AND this handler is bound — a chip that raises nothing is not offered.

parameters.name: RenderThrottle
parameters.description: Minimum time between two renders of a streamed answer. Default 50 ms. A Server circuit re-rendering per token is a render storm, so deltas arriving faster than this interval are folded into the message but not painted; the stream always renders once when it starts and once when it ends. Zero or a negative value renders every applied delta.

parameters.name: RenderWindowSize
parameters.description: How many of the newest turns are rendered; null (the default) renders every turn. A window keeps a very long transcript's DOM small, renders the contiguous tail and grows upwards by RenderWindowStep through the "Load older messages" control. Values below 10 are raised to 10 — a two-row window is a teaser, not a conversation.

parameters.name: RenderWindowStep
parameters.description: How many turns one "Load older messages" activation adds. Default 50, raised to at least 10.

parameters.name: ShowStop
parameters.description: Offer the built-in "Stop generating" control while a stream runs. Default true; a host that renders its own stop control (a composer, a toolbar) turns it off and calls StopAsync() itself.

parameters.name: Suggestions
parameters.description: Prompts offered by the empty state. They render only while the conversation has no turn AND OnSuggestion is bound.

examples.title: Stream an answer into the conversation
examples.code:
<TmAiConversation @ref="conversation" Messages="@messages" />

@code {
    private TmAiConversation conversation = default!;
    private readonly List<AiMessage> messages = new();

    private async Task SendAsync(string prompt)
    {
        messages.Add(new AiMessage { Role = AiMessageRole.User, Parts = { new AiTextPart(prompt) } });
        var answer = new AiMessage { Role = AiMessageRole.Assistant, Status = AiMessageStatus.Pending };
        messages.Add(answer);
        await conversation.StreamAsync(answer, client.StreamAsync(prompt));
    }
}

</TmAiConversation>

items.description: One turn of an AI conversation (a user prompt or the model's answer): the ordered parts rendered through the safe markdown view, the citation chips with a source preview, the source cards, the follow-up chips and the action toolbar (copy as plain text, regenerate with a version switcher, thumbs up/down with an optional reason, read aloud). A reasoning part renders through TmReasoningPanel (collapsed summary, live counter, steps and inspected sources) and consecutive tool-call parts collapse into one TmToolCallGroup (a single call renders as its own TmToolCallCard). The bubble mirrors itself for a user turn, and the three lifecycle states read differently: streaming streams with the package caret and marks the body busy, stopped shows a localized label, failed shows the error with Retry.

parameters.name: ActionsTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the whole built-in action toolbar with host actions. The built-in bar is a role=toolbar with a roving tabindex; a host template owns its own keyboard model, so it is rendered as plain content and must provide one if it renders more than one button.

parameters.name: ActiveVersionIndexChanged
parameters.description: Raised with the target zero-based version index when the reader steps through the regenerated versions. The component shows the chosen version immediately but never mutates AiMessage.ActiveVersionIndex: assign the index in the handler to persist the choice, and a host that changes the model's index itself wins over the reader's last step.

parameters.name: AvatarTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the default role glyph inside the avatar slot. The slot itself stays decorative (aria-hidden): the role is conveyed by the message's own accessible structure, so a host image here must not introduce a second name for the same turn.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: The message this block renders. Required: a null value renders an empty shell (the body is empty and no action is offered) instead of throwing, so a host can place the component before the first token arrives.

parameters.name: OnCitationClick
parameters.description: Raised with the source id when a citation chip is activated — after the built-in source preview opened, so a host can navigate away without losing the preview state it never sees.

parameters.name: OnFeedback
parameters.description: Raised with the rating when the reader presses a thumb. A negative rating is raised immediately (thumbs up/down must never require an explanation) and raised a second time with AiFeedback.Reason when the reader submits the optional reason.

parameters.name: OnFollowUp
parameters.description: Raised with the suggestion text when a follow-up chip is activated.

parameters.name: OnRegenerate
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks for another generation of this answer. The action renders only when a handler is bound, so no host gets a button that does nothing.

parameters.name: OnRetry
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks to retry a failed generation.

parameters.name: OnToolCallRetry
parameters.description: Raised with the tool call the reader asked to run again, from a failed call's Retry button — inside a single call's card or inside a grouped run. The buttons render only when a handler is bound, so no host gets a button that does nothing.

parameters.name: ReadAloud
parameters.description: Offer the "Read aloud" action, which speaks the answer's plain text through the browser's speechSynthesis. Default false. The action is hidden when the browser has no speech synthesis (feature-detected on first render) — never a dead button.

parameters.name: ShowActions
parameters.description: Render the action toolbar (copy, regenerate, read aloud, feedback). Default true; the bar itself is offered only for a finished turn (completed, stopped or failed), because there is nothing to copy, regenerate or rate while the answer is still arriving.

parameters.name: ShowAvatar
parameters.description: Render the avatar slot (the role glyph, or AvatarTemplate). Default true.

parameters.name: ShowFollowUps
parameters.description: Render the follow-up suggestions as chips under the answer. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowSources
parameters.description: Render the cited sources as cards in part order. Default true.

items.description: What a context window is made of: the system prompt, the tools, the memory, the files, the conversation and the tool results, measured against the model's budget. The presentation (Variant) changes only the PICTURE — one stacked bar (the default), a hundred cells over the budget so the free headroom is visible, or the core TmChart treemap. Every picture is decorative (aria-hidden); the legend table under it is the representation a reader, a screen reader and a copy/paste get, and it carries the label, the tokens, the whole percentage and the localized Required / Summarized / Omitted words of every section — never a colour-only cue. The total is a single role="meter" element carrying the invariant machine values and a localized aria-valuetext, so the amount is heard once (the visible read-out above it is sighted-only duplication). The percentages of the sections come from the largest-remainder split (ContextUsageMath.Shares), so they add up to exactly 100 %; a section with tokens whose rounded share is zero reads "< 1 %" and still paints a visible sliver. A section with Items expands into its entries through a native disclosure button, and a removable section or entry offers the localized Remove action. The component NEVER edits the snapshot: it reports the reader's intent through OnRemoveItem (the whole section when ContextUsageRemoval.Item is null, one entry otherwise) and OnCompact, and the host decides what to do; because the pressed control can disappear with the removal, the focus is handed back to the section's own disclosure button — or to the component root when that is gone too. The component is transport-agnostic and declares no motion at all: it renders the snapshot it is given and never polls. The ONE polite live region announces a budget CROSSING only, so a page load stays silent.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: The accessible name used when no visible heading names the panel, and the panel root's name. Null falls back to the localized "Context usage". A rendered Title always wins for the meter, so one control never carries two names.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the token counts and the percentages. Null means the current culture at render time. The machine-readable attributes (aria-valuenow / aria-valuemax) are always invariant — a culture's group separator would change the value a screen reader reads.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading's level in the page outline, clamped to 2–6. Default 3. The heading is only rendered when Title is set and ShowTitle is true.

parameters.name: OnCompact
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks for a compaction (summarise the optional parts). The action is rendered only when this callback is bound, and it is DISABLED while no section can be compacted (ContextUsageMath.IsCompactable), so a button is never offered that would do nothing.

parameters.name: OnRemoveItem
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks to drop something: something reported by a section with ContextUsageSection.CanRemove (the whole section — ContextUsageRemoval.Item is null) or an entry with ContextUsageItem.CanRemove. The action is rendered only when this callback is bound, so a read-only host offers no removal at all.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true; a host that already titles the card passes false and keeps naming the meter by AriaLabel or the localized default.

parameters.name: Snapshot
parameters.description: The snapshot to render — the budget, the sections and the cache-hit share. Null (or a snapshot with no sections) renders the localized empty state instead of an empty chart. The component never mutates it and never polls: a host pushes a new instance as the conversation grows.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The visible heading of the panel and, through aria-labelledby, the name of the meter. Null renders no heading; the panel and the meter are then named by AriaLabel or the localized default.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: How the context is presented. Default ContextUsageVariant.Bar (one stacked bar); the grid shows a hundred cells over the budget and the treemap draws the sections through the core TmChart. The legend table, the meter and the empty state are identical in every variant.

examples.title: A context window a host measures

<TmContextUsage Snapshot="@snapshot"
                Title="Context window"
                OnRemoveItem="OnRemoveAsync"
                OnCompact="CompactAsync" />

@code {
    private ContextUsageSnapshot snapshot = new()
    {
        BudgetTokens = 16_000,
        CacheHit = 0.62,
        Sections =
        [
            new("system", "System prompt") { Kind = ContextUsageKind.System, Tokens = 1_200, IsRequired = true },
            new("files", "Files")
            {
                Kind = ContextUsageKind.Files,
                Tokens = 5_000,
                CanRemove = true,
                Items = [new ContextUsageItem("contract", "Contract.pdf") { Tokens = 4_000, CanRemove = true }],
            },

    };

    private Task OnRemoveAsync(ContextUsageRemoval removal)
    {
        // removal.Item is null for a whole section, otherwise it names the single entry.
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    }

    private Task CompactAsync() => Task.CompletedTask;
}

items.description: The models tried for ONE request, in the order they were tried, as a flow that ends in an Answer node — every attempt with its result, the reason it failed or was skipped, how long it took and when — plus an edit mode in which a reader reorders the chain, adds a model from the host's catalogue and removes one. The surface renders the run it is given and never polls or mutates the host's data: in the RUN view it only reads Attempts, and in the EDIT view it keeps its own working copy of Chain and reports every change through ChainChanged (a reorder through the shared TmSortableList, which supplies the pointer drag AND its keyboard and menu alternatives, WCAG 2.5.7). Accessibility: every attempt is a labelled node of an ordered list, its result is an ICON plus a localized WORD plus a tone (colour is never the only carrier), a failure or a skip always prints its reason, and the decorative arrows are aria-hidden because the list already carries the order. The table view carries exactly the same facts without the geometry, so a screen-reader, keyboard-only or phone reader loses nothing. ONE polite live region speaks only when the reader adds or removes a model — a reorder is narrated by the sortable list itself, so nothing is announced twice.

parameters.name: Attempts
parameters.description: The attempts, in the order they were tried. Each entry is one node of the flow; null or empty renders the localized empty state, and a null entry inside the list is skipped. The component never mutates the list.

parameters.name: AvailableModels
parameters.description: The host's model catalogue, from which the editor offers what is NOT already in the chain. Null or empty renders the localized "no models are available" note and a disabled Add button.

parameters.name: Chain
parameters.description: The models in fallback order, two-way bound with ChainChanged (@bind-Chain). Null (the default) derives the chain from Attempts, which is what an editor opened over a finished run shows. A pinned list is copied, never mutated: the reader's reorder reports a NEW list through ChainChanged.

parameters.name: ChainChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new chain whenever the reader reorders, adds or removes a model.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the latencies and the attempt times. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Whether the surface reports the run or edits the chain. Default View. The host owns this switch (it is not two-way): the component never changes it on its own.

parameters.name: Policy
parameters.description: The rule the chain follows, two-way bound with PolicyChanged (@bind-Policy). Default Pin, so an unset policy never falls back to another model by accident. The editor offers the three policies as a segmented radio group; the run view reports the value as a word.

parameters.name: PolicyChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new policy when the reader picks one in the editor.

parameters.name: ShowPolicy
parameters.description: Whether the policy is shown at all. Default true — the run view prints it as a read-out and the editor offers the radio group.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Fallback chain"); the heading also names the surface, so the name a reader hears is the one they see.

parameters.name: ViewMode
parameters.description: The run presentation, two-way bound with ViewModeChanged (@bind-ViewMode). Default Flow. It applies to the run view; the editor has its own presentation.

parameters.name: ViewModeChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new presentation when the reader uses the View switcher.

examples.title: A run a host reports, and the editor over the same chain
The attempts a host recorded

notes: The run view only reads Attempts; the editor keeps its own copy of Chain and reports every change through ChainChanged (never mutating the host list).
The editor reorders through the shared TmSortableList, so the pointer drag, the keyboard grab/move/drop and the per-row move menu all work (WCAG 2.5.7).
Adding is limited to AvailableModels that are not already in the chain; removing and reordering keep the chain a sequence of distinct models.
ONE polite live region announces an add and a remove; a reorder is narrated by the sortable list itself, so nothing is announced twice.
The table view (ViewMode=Table) carries every attempt, result, reason, latency and time as text — the flow is never the only way to read the run.
An unmeasured latency is never invented: the flow omits it and the table says "not measured".

items.description: An orchestrator's fan-out as ONE card: a summary line (how much finished, what it cost, when it should be over) and a grid of tiles — one tile per unit of work, with its worker, its state, its attempt count and a live countdown to its estimate. The surface renders the task list it is given and never polls or mutates anything: the host owns the data and the transport, the component owns its view. The injected TimeProvider drives the countdown AND the ticker that repaints it, so a test with a fake clock closes a second without sleeping and a finished fan-out arms no timer at all. The grid is an APG grid: ONE tab stop (a roving tabindex), the arrow keys walk the tiles in reading order, Home/End stay inside the current row and Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End jump across the whole grid, PageUp/PageDown jump a page of rows. A tile is a native <button>, so Enter and Space activate it exactly once with no emulation (docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md). A state is never carried by colour alone: the tile paints an icon, a localized WORD and a tone. The detail follows the tile the reader focused (or pointed at) and carries the Retry and Cancel actions — the same actions a host would put on a row menu, reachable without a pointer. Hundreds of tasks mount a bounded window of tiles while the grid still declares its full aria-rowcount and every mounted row keeps its real aria-rowindex, so what a screen reader counts is the grid, not the window.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: How many tiles sit on one grid row, clamped to 1–8. Default 4. The value is also written onto the root as --tm-fan-out-columns, so the stylesheet lays the rows out with the same number the C# window uses.

parameters.name: Compact
parameters.description: Whether the compact presentation is used: a tile keeps its label, its state word and its attempt badge and drops the countdown and the worker line. Default false. The grid keys, the detail and the actions are unchanged — compact hides information, never a way to act.

parameters.name: CostFormatter
parameters.description: Formats a cost given in MICRO-UNITS (1,000,000 is 1.00 of the currency). Null uses AiCostFormatter with Culture — the culture's own currency, with micro-unit precision below one hundredth of a unit. A host with a credit price model overrides it.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the costs and the clock times. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time. The countdowns are clock-style (m:ss) on purpose and are not localized.

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: The state filter, two-way bound with FilterChanged (@bind-Filter). Default All. A host that pins it keeps control: the reader's pick reports the change and the next render from the host decides.

parameters.name: FilterChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new filter when the reader picks one in the filter bar.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: OnCancel
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks to cancel a task — the action lives in the tile's detail and is offered only while CanCancel holds. The component does not change the task.

parameters.name: OnRetry
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks for a retry of a failed task — the action lives in the tile's detail and is offered only while CanRetry holds. The component does not change the task: the host owns the data and re-renders with the retried value.

parameters.name: ShowFilter
parameters.description: Whether the state filter bar is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowSummary
parameters.description: Whether the summary line is rendered. Default true. It carries the finished / running / failed counts, the total of the priced tasks and the estimate of the last active one.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: Tasks
parameters.description: The units of work the orchestrator split the job into. Each tile is one entry; the summary counts the same list. Null or empty renders the localized empty state. The component never mutates the list and never reorders it — the grid paints the host's order, because that order is the host's own progress.

parameters.name: TimeProvider
parameters.description: The clock the countdowns and the repaint ticker read. Null uses the container's TimeProvider and falls back to System — the host's clock always wins over the machine's.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Fan-out"); the heading also names the card, so the name a reader hears is the one they see.

parameters.name: VisibleTaskLimit
parameters.description: How many tiles may be mounted at once. Default 60; 0 (or a negative value) mounts the whole filtered list. Above the limit the grid mounts a window of whole rows that follows the focused tile, while aria-rowcount keeps declaring the filtered total — hundreds of tasks stay scrollable and cheap.

examples.title: A fan-out a host feeds from its queue
The tasks a host builds

notes: The surface renders the snapshot it is given; it never polls, fetches or mutates a task.
The injected TimeProvider drives the countdown and the repaint ticker: a test with a fake clock closes a second without sleeping, and a finished fan-out arms no timer.
Columns is the layout authority: the C# window and the stylesheet read the same number, so a host that needs fewer tiles on a phone binds Columns rather than relying on a container query.
One polite live region announces a filter change, a moved focus and a retry or cancel request; the tiles themselves are native buttons with one roving tab stop.

items.description: Renders untrusted markdown (an AI answer, a tool result, a system note) through the package's safe pipeline: raw HTML is escaped instead of rendered, only http/https/mailto and relative link targets survive (everything else collapses to '#'), images are limited to absolute http(s), every link carries target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow", code blocks get a copy affordance and cite: links become citation chips that raise OnCitationClick. The rendered HTML is cached against the last input, so a parent re-render with unchanged text does not re-run Markdig.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: CodeBlockTemplate
parameters.description: Optional host renderer for a code block, replacing the built-in <pre><code> plus copy affordance (for example with syntax-highlighted markup). The returned HTML is trusted verbatim, so the host owns its escaping: pass context.Code through HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode. Pass a stable reference — a cached field, a static method or a method group — because the render cache compares the delegate's Method and Target, not the delegate instance.

parameters.name: Markdown
parameters.description: The markdown to render. It is untrusted model output: the component renders it through the safe markdown pipeline (raw HTML disabled, http/https/mailto/relative allowlist, hardened links), so a hostile answer cannot execute markup. Tables become a keyboard-reachable named region and code blocks get a keyboard-reachable scroller plus a copy button that announces through a live region.

parameters.name: OnCitationClick
parameters.description: Raised with the source id when a citation chip is activated, so the host can open the source preview (the chips are rendered for markdown links written as [1](cite:<sourceId>)).

examples.title: Render an assistant answer with citation clicks
examples.code:
<TmMarkdownView Markdown="@message.Text"
                OnCitationClick="id => ShowSourcePreview(message.FindSource(id))" />

examples.title: Replace the code-block markup with syntax highlighting
examples.code:
<TmMarkdownView Markdown="@answer"
                CodeBlockTemplate="ctx => Highlighter.RenderHtml(ctx.Code, ctx.Language)" />

items.description: Picks the model a conversation runs on: the trigger names the chosen model plus its state tags, and the popup lists the host's catalogue as a role="listbox" whose every row compares the models on speed, quality, price per million input tokens and context window — as a bar AND as the number in words, because a bar alone is colour-only information. The list is grouped by GroupBy (provider, family or nothing) and searched live; the hits are marked by TmHighlightedText and a group with no surviving model disappears instead of leaving an empty heading. A model that does not report a value renders no bar and no chip — "not reported" is never painted as a zero. The selected model's reasoning options (extended thinking, effort levels) sit ABOVE the list, never inside an option: an option is a leaf of the listbox and may not contain a switch or a radio. The whole answer is Selection (@bind-Selection): the model id, the extended-thinking switch and the reasoning-effort level. Keyboard: the trigger is a native button; focus moves into the search field, which is the popup's combobox carrying aria-activedescendant, and with ShowSearch off the listbox itself owns the arrows, Enter (keydown), Space (keyup) and type-ahead. The trigger is named by its own visible text (a visually hidden "Model:" prefix plus the model, its provider and every state tag), the listbox by the localized "Models" label, and one polite live region announces the pick, the reasoning changes and the search match count. On a phone the popup is a bottom sheet.

parameters.name: AriaLabel
parameters.description: An optional accessible name for the trigger. Null (the default) lets the trigger's own visible text name it — the localized "Model:" prefix plus the model, its provider and every state tag — and the root group is named by the localized "Model". Setting it replaces that name; the state tags are then exposed through the trigger's description, so a deprecated or reasoning model is still announced.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: CloseOnSelect
parameters.description: Whether a pick closes the popup. Default true (the combobox behaviour). false keeps the list open so the reader can compare models; the picked row is then marked as selected in place.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the prices, the estimate and the speed/quality numbers. Null means the current culture at render time.

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Disables the trigger and every control of the popup: nothing opens and nothing is raised.

parameters.name: EstimatedPromptTokens
parameters.description: How many prompt tokens the next request is expected to send. When set (and the selected model reports an input price) the panel renders the estimated prompt cost, formatted with the culture's currency. Null renders no estimate.

parameters.name: GroupBy
parameters.description: How the list is grouped. Default AiModelGroupBy.Provider; a model that does not report the property lands in the localized "Other" group and is never dropped.

parameters.name: LayoutMode
parameters.description: The layout the popup presentation resolves from. Auto follows the viewport; a forced value never measures, so a test can render a mode without a DOM.

parameters.name: MobilePresentation
parameters.description: How the popup presents on a narrow viewport. Default Auto — the anchored popover on a wide layout and a bottom sheet on a phone.

parameters.name: Models
parameters.description: The catalogue to choose from. The component never mutates it; the host's order is the reading order and a group keeps the order its models arrive in. Null or empty renders an empty state rather than an empty listbox.

parameters.name: PriceFormatter
parameters.description: Formats a money amount — a price per million tokens and the prompt estimate. Null uses AiCostFormatter with Culture (the culture's own currency and symbol position). A host with credits or a fixed exchange rate overrides it.

parameters.name: SearchPlaceholder
parameters.description: The placeholder of the search field. Null uses the localized default.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: The current answer, two-way bound with SelectionChanged (@bind-Selection). Null renders the placeholder trigger. A host may keep the picker uncontrolled: a pick still renders and the host's stale parameter never overwrites it.

parameters.name: SelectionChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the whole new selection: a picked model (the reasoning options at the model's defaults), a toggled extended thinking or a chosen effort level.

parameters.name: ShowCapabilities
parameters.description: Whether a row renders the model's capability chips. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowContextWindow
parameters.description: Whether a row renders its context window chip. Default true; an unreported window renders no chip.

parameters.name: ShowEffort
parameters.description: Whether the selected model's reasoning-effort control is offered when the model reports levels. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowExtendedThinking
parameters.description: Whether the selected model's extended-thinking switch is offered when the model supports it. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowPrice
parameters.description: Whether a row renders its input price bar and value. Default true; an unreported price renders neither (an unknown price is never painted as free).

parameters.name: ShowQuality
parameters.description: Whether a row renders its quality bar and value. Default true; a model that reports no score renders neither.

parameters.name: ShowSearch
parameters.description: Whether the search field is rendered. Default true. Without it the listbox is the popup's tab stop and offers type-ahead instead.

parameters.name: ShowSpeed
parameters.description: Whether a row renders its speed bar and value. Default true; a model that reports no score renders neither.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered inside the popup. Default true; the listbox keeps its name either way.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The visible heading of the popup (and of the bottom sheet, when the popup presents as one). Null uses the localized "Choose a model". The listbox is named separately by the localized "Models" label, so the title is not spoken twice.

examples.title: A catalogue with a bound selection

<TmModelPicker Models="@models"
               @bind-Selection="selection"
               EstimatedPromptTokens="100000"
               PriceFormatter="FormatPrice" />

@code {
    private AiModelSelection? selection = new("gpt-4o");
    private IReadOnlyList<AiModelInfo> models = [
        new("gpt-4o", "GPT-4o") { Provider = "OpenAI", ContextWindow = 128_000, SpeedScore = 4, QualityScore = 5, InputPricePerMillion = 3m },
        new("gpt-4o-mini", "GPT-4o mini") { Provider = "OpenAI", ContextWindow = 128_000, SpeedScore = 5, QualityScore = 3, InputPricePerMillion = 0.15m },
    ];
}

examples.title: Grouped by family, with the reasoning options
examples.code:
<TmModelPicker Models="@models"
               GroupBy="AiModelGroupBy.Family"
               @bind-Selection="selection" />

examples.title: A compact toolbar picker without the search field
examples.code:
<TmModelPicker Models="@models"
               ShowSearch="false"
               ShowCapabilities="false"
               ShowQuality="false"
               ShowEffort="false"
               @bind-Selection="selection" />

examples.title: Comparing without closing the list
examples.code:
<TmModelPicker Models="@models" CloseOnSelect="false" SelectionChanged="OnSelection" />

@code {
    private void OnSelection(AiModelSelection? value)
    {
        // Every change lands here, including the reasoning options of the selected model.
    }
}

items.description: Several attempts at the SAME piece of work, side by side: one column per attempt with its state, its score, its own summary, the body the host renders and the votes it collected — and a winner the reader picks and confirms. The surface renders the attempts it is given and never mutates them and never invents a score: the best attempt is the host's explicit pick (BestAttemptId) when it names one, otherwise ParallelAttemptRanking resolves the highest score, so the column badge, the comparison table and a test can never disagree. Picking a winner is deliberately TWO steps. The native radios of one shared name are the choice — the arrow keys walk them natively, with no key emulation — and a pick asks for confirmation before OnSelect fires, so a stray arrow key can never replace a recorded result. The confirmation lives in a named group, the pick is announced once through the surface's ONE polite live region, and the focus returns to the radio that opened the question. The columns are a horizontal scroll-snap track: a narrow container turns them into a carousel with no JavaScript and no second layout engine. The comparison table below repeats every number as text, which is the surface a screen reader or a phone reads.

parameters.name: Attempts
parameters.description: The attempts to compare, in the host's own order. Each one is a column and a row of the comparison table; the surface never reorders them, so the host's order stays the reader's order. Null or empty renders the localized empty state.

parameters.name: BestAttemptId
parameters.description: The host's explicit pick of the best attempt. When it names one of Attempts that attempt wears the "Best" mark whatever its score; when it names nothing (or something absent) the highest score decides. Null by default.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: ConfirmSelection
parameters.description: Whether a pick asks for confirmation before it becomes the winner. Default true — the safe default, so a stray arrow key inside the radio group cannot replace a recorded result. A host that wants a one-step choice passes false and the pick raises OnSelect immediately.

parameters.name: ContentTemplate
parameters.description: The host's own body for one attempt — a diff, a document, a code block, plain prose. Rendered inside that attempt's column, so every body stays bound to its own attempt. Null renders no body.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the scores. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time. It never rescales a score: the host's scale is the host's.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: OnSelect
parameters.description: Raised with the attempt id once the reader CONFIRMED it as the result. A host that only needs the value can bind SelectedAttemptId instead; this callback is the command channel (record the winner, start the next step).

parameters.name: SelectedAttemptId
parameters.description: The confirmed winner, two-way bound with SelectedAttemptIdChanged (@bind-SelectedAttemptId). Its radio is checked and its column carries the "Chosen" mark. A host that BINDS it delegates the decision: the reader's confirmation reports the change and the next render from the host decides. A host that only PINS it (a value without SelectedAttemptIdChanged) keeps control: the confirmed pick is shown until the host renders again, and then the pinned value is restored. A host that sets neither keeps the reader's pick.

parameters.name: SelectedAttemptIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the newly confirmed winner (never a merely picked one).

parameters.name: ShowComparison
parameters.description: Whether the comparison table is rendered. Default true — it is the text alternative of the columns (the same numbers as a table), so a host hides it only when it renders its own.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Parallel attempts").

examples.title: Three drafts with a confirmed winner
